title: Nvidia closes in on Hugging Face acquisition
summary: Nvidia is reportedly nearing a $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face, a leading platform for open-source AI models. The deal aims to strengthen Nvidia's position in the open-source AI ecosystem, counter competition from closed AI labs developing their own chips, and re-enter the cloud computing market. Hugging Face's CEO has publicly aligned with Nvidia's open-source advocacy, and the acquisition would provide financial stability and growth opportunities for Hugging Face amid rising competition in AI infrastructure.
key_points: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, valuing the company at over $13 billion.
Hugging Face is a key hub for open-source AI models, and its acquisition would bolster Nvidia's foothold in open-source AI.
The deal helps Nvidia counter competition from closed AI labs (e.g., OpenAI, Google, Amazon) developing their own AI chips to reduce reliance on Nvidia's hardware.
Nvidia has invested heavily in open-source AI models to maintain market dominance in AI chips.
Hugging Face's CEO, Clem Delangue, has publicly supported Nvidia's open-source AI initiatives, including a joint letter urging U.S. government support for open models.
The acquisition could re-establish Nvidia in cloud computing by leveraging Hugging Face's existing infrastructure for AI model deployment.
Nvidia may use Hugging Face to monetize unused cloud computing capacity from its customer deals.
Hugging Face's revenue grew from $100 million to $150 million in two months, nearing profitability, but the $13 billion valuation represents a significant premium.
Hugging Face previously rejected a $500 million Nvidia investment offer at a $7 billion valuation but may now accept the buyout for growth and financial stability.
The deal reflects broader consolidation in AI infrastructure, as seen with Stripe's recent $7 billion acquisition of OpenRouter.
